stem: The most common areas of nomadic herding are –
expl: Nomadic herding is a practiced of moving from one place to another with cattle in search of pasture. Nomadic pastoralism is commonly practised in regions with arid land around the world, especially in the steppe lands of the agricultural zone of Eurasia. Nomadic herding still exists in the world in the areas of Central Asia, Africa and South America.

stem: 'Transhumance' refers to –

options.label: b
options.text: Human migration in search of job

options.label: c
options.text: Seasonal movement of people and their herds from the valley to the mountain and vice versa

expl: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of people with their livestock from one grazing ground to another such as from lowlands to highlands, with the change of seasons. Pastoral communities in the Himalayas, such as the Bhotiya, Bakarwal and Gaddi traditionally been practicing livestock herding by migrating to more suitable pastures on a seasonal basis in India.

stem: Which of the following is considered to be the most recent?
expl: Cro- Magnon humans are considered to be the most recent among the above mentioned Homo sapiens species. They are the immediate ancestors of modern Homo sapiens. The first specimen of Cro- Magnon human remains was found in 1868 in Dordogne, France. The Cro-Magnon man, an early Homo sapiens (the species to which modern humans belong) is considered to have lived about 40,000 to 10000 years ago.

stem: The first bird is believed to have appeared on the surface of the earth-

stem: Which racial group has the largest number of members?
expl: Presently, the Caucasoids are considered the largest racial group in the world. The color of eyes, among the Caucasoids, ranges from light blue to dark brown and hair vanies from straight to wavy. The skull index is more than 80. Howell & Smith classified the race into three classes : Nordic, Alpine and Mediterranean. The Caucasoid race has the largest number of members in the world.
